Thanks for the context. A few notes from deal desk / finance POV:

- Net-60 is outside our standard private-offer payment window (we typically accept Net-30 for marketplace billing). We have approved Net-45 on rare occasions with credit checks. Net-60 carries collection risk and will require AP credit sign-off (Lauren).
- Rev-share carve-in to a partner: Marketplace payouts can be routed but this is a commercial exception. Our standard commission cap to partners on private offers is 8%. VectorNet is requesting 9% for 12 months — that exceeds the cap by 1%.

Because this is both a longer-than-normal payment term and a >8% partner carve, I recommend executive approval. If leadership approves, we will:
1) Require a one-time billing guarantee (pre-authorized PO or a partial upfront) or a short-term credit review.
2) Limit the carve-in to 12 months then revert to standard grid.
3) Legal to add a specific residency clause as requested (we should scope it with Legal).

Marissa — any preference on escalation? If we escalate to execs, we should include expected ARR, partner name, and a recommended concession plan (I suggest approving 9% for 12 months if we get a 25% upfront payment or PO).

Ben
Deal Desk Manager
